scope: 48 submissions in scope: 24 Privacy-only + 24 entered in both tracks.
45 readable. Not readable, shown as gaps: Obscura (no repo submitted), Cloister (repo on GitLab, which the review workspace could not reach), ZapOut (GitHub repo private or deleted on 9 Nov).

The review reads each repo as of 9 Nov, not as at the 00:00 IST 5 Nov deadline. Projects whose latest commit is after the deadline are flagged in the table (column "After deadline"); judges' scores were based on the deadline state.
countingRule: Counts are use in the project's own code or dependency files (.rs .ts .tsx .js .mjs .py .go .toml .json .html .sh .yml, package.json, Cargo.toml, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod). Excluded from the search: node_modules, build output, lockfiles, minified bundles, docs/, evidence/, and the shared template files most teams copied from the event (AGENTS.md, AGENTS.txt, CLAUDE.md, *llms*.txt, docs/briefs/). Those templates name Noir Wallet, Nym, WebZjs, Zallet, zkool and FROST, so a raw text search over-counts badly (for example 22 repos mention Noir Wallet; 11 use it).

projects.title: Z-Pay — shielded checkout, without a merchant app
zcash-now: A keyless MCP server and llms.txt that keep AI coding agents current on Zcash, so a developer new to Zcash gets code that works on today's NU7 testnet the first time

nymDetails: Built-in details: Veylor (lwd-nym crate opening a lightwalletd gRPC channel over a fresh Nym tunnel), Ghost Layer (two nym-socks5-client instances with different exits), Oboro (nym:// tunnel via oboro-node, nymtech/nym git dependency), ColdTrail, MaZe and Z402 (@nymproject/mix-fetch in the browser), Zeno Wallet (SOCKS5 to a local nym-socks5-client).
webzjsNote: Z-Pay builds WebZjs from source at commit a50df944, adds patches/webzjs-checkout.patch (pczt_send returning a txid, ZIP-321 payment with memo) and ships it as a MetaMask snap. The zcash-now entries warn agents that WebZjs is not on npm and has no Ironwood support.

upstreamDescription: Found by GitHub search for PRs, issues and comments authored by every commit author of each repo (plus the repo owner) since 15 Oct 2026, keeping repos the team doesn't own. Links the teams merely cite (for example zcash/librustzcash #1484, zcash/lightwallet-protocol #25, NoirWallet/noir-wallet #53, zcash/zips #387) were written by others and are excluded. Unrelated open-source work by the same people (NEAR, design PRs) is excluded.

upstreamCaveats.Secret Bankroll: Secret Bankroll's PR is to AlwaysHungrie/salts-agent, which is probably a teammate's repo (the team's demo video is on @Always_Hungrie_'s X account), so present it with that caveat.

frictionNote: Keyword reading of each repo's FEEDBACK.md. Coarse; use as a pointer, not a score.

findings.text: ZIP 321 (payment request URIs, 26 projects), ZIP 317 (fees, 25) and ZIP 316 (unified addresses, 13) are the working set. Memos are near universal in code even though only 7 projects cite ZIP 302; teams use them as order IDs, receipts and agent commands.

findings.lead: Selective disclosure is the biggest unmet need.
findings.text: Vouch, Ghost Layer and Zeno Wallet cite ZIP 311 (draft). Zeno reports the pinned crates don't implement it. Vouch and Z-Solvency reuse Valar's voting circuits to prove "at least X ZEC" without a viewing key.

findings.lead: Agent custody pulls in FROST and PCZT.
findings.text: Ironclad (ZIP 312 + ZIP 374 + ZIP 2005), Zealed and Pactora run FROST; seven projects build PCZTs. Spending limits enforced in code outside the model are the common pattern across agent projects.

findings.lead: Ironwood and NU7 knowledge is scattered.
findings.text: Teams cite ZIPs 258, 259, 229, 318, 326, 2003, 2005 and 2009 to pin heights and formats. Zec Start's feedback asks for one "what is Ironwood" page; both zcash-now entries exist to keep agents current.

findings.lead: Missing primitives show at the edges.
findings.text: zkLane needs relative timelocks (ZIPs 68/112) to close channels on chain; Finity and Mirage work around TEX addresses (ZIP 320); zshagun points to ZIP 324 for payment links.
Seven projects built it in. zingo-cli's Nym-by-default build made four teams turn it off to ship a demo, and three teams list it as friction in their feedback.
One project patched it from source; several evaluated it and moved to zcash-devtool, zkool or Noir Wallet.

findings.lead: CLIs beat SDKs on day one.
findings.text: zcash-devtool (15) and zkool (10) are the most-used ways to reach Zcash; Munim writes that zcash-devtool "built and synced the first time" where SDKs did not.

findings.lead: Upstream contributions are few but concrete.
findings.text: Four teams filed 7 PRs/issues during the hack (zcash-devtool memo walkthrough PR #271 and memo-app issue #272, Bitrefill MCP issues, a frost-zec policy co-signer request). Three more drafted upstream issues or patches in their repos without filing them.
